canonical_topic: Geographic risk gradient of acid rain from coal plants
definition: Acid rain exposure risk from coal mining and coal power generation is not uniform — it is concentrated near the source and fades with distance.
core_idea: Populations located near coal mines and power plants, downwind of plant emissions, or downstream of related discharges face the greatest acid rain risk, with severity declining as distance from the source increases; the author notes acid rain is not harmful at low concentrations.
key_points: Highest-risk locations: near the mine/plant, downwind of it, or downstream from it
Risk magnitude decreases with distance from the source
Acid rain is not considered dangerous in small concentrations
relationships: Sets up the motivation for sulfur removal via coal washing and flue gas desulfurization
caveats: Acid rain risk is not an all-or-nothing hazard — it scales with proximity and concentration
